messages:
maria: FYI — seeing intermittent SSL certificate verification failures on Windows with the async Python SDK (3.11). Sync client on same host works fine. Error: ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED]

tkim: Can you paste a tiny repro and the traceback?

maria: Sure, minimal repro below (using aiohttp under the hood):
```python
import os, ssl
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

os.environ['SSL_CERT_FILE'] = r'C:\Users\maria\AppData\Local\certs\cacert.pem'

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(api_key='sk-...') as c:
        await c.generate('hello')

asyncio.run(main())
```
Traceback snippet: ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:1007)

andrew: Which OpenSSL is your Python using? `python -c "import ssl; print(ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION)"`

maria: Output: OpenSSL 3.0.9  (Library: libcrypto 3.0.9) — CPython 3.11.4 64-bit on Win10

tkim: Interesting — sync client (requests) tends to honor REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and certifi; aiohttp/ssl may not pick up REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE on Windows the same way. Two quick workarounds: 1) create ssl context with cafile=certifi.where() and pass to aiohttp, or 2) set SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where() at process start.

maria: Confirmed — setting REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE did nothing, but `os.environ['SSL_CERT_FILE'] = certifi.where()` before creating client fixed it for me.

andrew: We should track this — it looks like parity gaps between sync/async clients: (a) env CA handling (b) retry/backoff parity — async client currently doesn't mirror the sync RetryPolicy so 429s/connection hickups bubble to callers.

tkim: I'll open a GH issue. Short-term patch idea: accept `ca_certs` param in AsyncClient.__init__ (fallback order: explicit param -> SSL_CERT_FILE env -> certifi.where()), and plumb an identical RetryPolicy for async. Also add typing for AsyncClient in stubs — typing gaps surfaced in mypy on py3.8/3.11 matrix.

maria: Please also add a tiny Windows-only integration test (skip unless sys.platform == 'win32') so CI doesn't regress. I'll add our repro to the test matrix for 3.8–3.12.

devex-bot: PR opened by tkim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/438 — runs CI on windows-latest and linux.

andrew: Awesome — :thumbsup: When you open the PR, mention the migration note for Windows users and the env var behavior, and call out that certifi is a safe default.

tkim: Will do. Filing GH issue #432 with logs, traceback, and repro.

maria: Thanks — saved me hours of debugging. If anyone on the team has a windows VM spare, please sanity-check the PR on 3.8 and 3.11.
